question: Round 4, combine the survivors and test them for bias and fragility. Is round 3's earnings filter (u_sue0) a real edge or just the effect of dropping stocks the SEC ticker list no longer has (delisted names, which skew to losers)? Do skipping RS 99 (p_cap98) and ranking tight bases (e_tight) add to it, and do the results hold when each setting is nudged?

variants.name: ctrl_hasdata
variants.why: CONTROL: only names with fundamentals data, no earnings condition. Whatever u_sue0 gains beyond this is the earnings signal; the rest is the data-coverage bias

variants.name: u_sue0
variants.why: round 3 winner, repeated in this run

variants.name: u_sue_m025
variants.why: sensitivity: a slightly looser surprise floor

variants.name: u_sue_p025
variants.why: sensitivity: a slightly stricter surprise floor

variants.name: c_sue0_cap98_tight_spy3
variants.why: all three + the stricter SPY filter
